items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The code is formatted cleanly, but the error message misleads. Prefetch() raises ValueError("Cannot filter a query once a slice has been taken.") before any filtering happens, and that text copies the filter() TypeError message instead of describing the restriction.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: This makes the reported limitation an enforced rule instead of fixing it. The core prefetch path (related_descriptors.py) is untouched and no helper was added. A later fix would have to undo this guard, and the agent's new test locks in the wrong behavior.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It rejects a valid use case (Post.objects.all()[:3]) up front instead of supporting it. Hidden tests fail: F2P 0/4, starting with PrefetchLimitTests.test_foreignkey_reverse. It is fail-fast, but it raises an error for input the issue says should work.

items.name: Per-parent slice semantics for open/bounded slices
items.name_zh: 开放/有界切片按父对象分区
items.evidence: No per-parent slicing at all: no Window or RowNumber, no partition_by, no handling of low/high marks. Every sliced queryset gets `if queryset.query.is_sliced: raise ValueError(...)`, so neither qs[n:] nor qs[n:m] is supported.
